title: Michelin Star Hawker in Singapore: Where to Eat (2026)
description: Singapore’s only Michelin star hawker stall, from S$8 a bowl, what happened to Hawker Chan, five Bib Gourmand hawkers and the cheapest starred lunch.
h1: Michelin Star Hawker Food in Singapore: Where to Eat for Under S$10
summary: The one hawker stall with a star, the Bib Gourmand stalls nearby and the cheapest starred lunch.
body:
One hawker stall in Singapore holds a Michelin star: Hill Street Tai Hwa Pork Noodle, in the MICHELIN Guide Singapore 2026, where a bowl of bak chor mee costs from {{dinner:hill-street-tai-hwa-pork-noodle}}. Hawker Chan lost its star in 2021. Dozens more hawker stalls hold a Bib Gourmand for good value. Prices checked {{checked}}.

Singapore was the first place the MICHELIN Guide gave a star to a hawker stall, in its first Singapore edition in 2016. Ten years on, Hill Street Tai Hwa is the only Singapore Michelin star hawker stall, and the cheapest starred meal anywhere in the world. Below are the city’s cheapest starred meals, the hawker stall itself, five Bib Gourmand hawkers worth the trip, and the cheapest starred lunch for when you want air conditioning and a tablecloth.

The cheapest Michelin star meals in Singapore

Singapore has {{cheapN_singapore}} starred restaurants. Ranked by the cheapest meal each one serves, the hawker stall sits far below the rest; after it come weekday set lunches at one-star restaurants. Restaurant prices in Singapore are quoted “++”, before a 10% service charge and 9% GST; hawker prices include everything.

{{table:cheapest-singapore}}

Hill Street Tai Hwa Pork Noodle

What to order: bak chor mee, the stall’s only dish: springy noodles tossed to order in black vinegar, chilli and lard, then topped with minced pork, sliced pork, liver, meatballs, dumplings and a piece of fried sole fish. You choose the noodle (thin mee pok is the classic), dry or soup, and the size. The stall dropped its smallest S$6 bowl in 2024, so bowls now start at {{dinner:hill-street-tai-hwa-pork-noodle}}.

The queue: long, and slow, because every bowl is made one at a time. At weekend lunchtimes expect to wait an hour or more; mid-afternoon on a weekday is usually quickest. You queue, order and pay at the counter, then wait for your bowl.

Where: Block 466 Crawford Lane, a coffee shop near Lavender MRT. It has held its star in every Singapore guide since 2016. Its MICHELIN Guide page has the latest opening hours.

What happened to Hawker Chan

Hawker Chan, the Chinatown Complex stall famous for soy sauce chicken rice at about S$2 a plate, won a star alongside Hill Street Tai Hwa in 2016 and was for years called the cheapest Michelin star meal in the world. After it opened branches across Asia, it was left out of the Singapore guide published in September 2021: the Hawker Chan Michelin star was gone, and the stall isn’t in the guide today. The original stall still sells its chicken rice. For the rest of the world’s cheapest starred meals, see the cheapest Michelin star meals in the world.

Five Bib Gourmand hawkers to try

The Bib Gourmand is the MICHELIN Guide’s award for good cooking at a moderate price, and in Singapore most of its Bib Gourmands are hawker stalls. It isn’t a star (see Bib Gourmand vs Michelin star), but it is the guide’s own shortlist of the hawker food it rates. Five of them, all in the current guide:

  • Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice, Maxwell Food Centre: poached chicken with springy skin and rice cooked in chicken fat and stock. The queue is part of the visit.
  • Margaret Drive Sin Kee Chicken Rice: a second chicken rice, made the same way for decades, with a sharp ginger sauce.
  • Singapore Fried Hokkien Mee: egg noodles and rice vermicelli fried with prawns and squid in a deep seafood stock. Unusually for a hawker, it opens from the afternoon until late.
  • Jalan Sultan Prawn Mee: more than 70 years of prawn noodles, dry with sambal or in a rich prawn broth.
  • Chey Sua Carrot Cake: radish cake fried to order on one side until crisp, soft and steaming on the other.

The cheapest starred lunch with a tablecloth

For a starred meal at a table, with service, go at lunch. The cheapest set lunch at a starred restaurant in Singapore is at {{cheapLunchName_singapore}}, for {{cheapLunchPrice_singapore}} ++. Lei Garden, the Cantonese dining room at CHIJMES, serves a lunch set for {{lunch:lei-garden}} ++, with dim sum on its lunch menu. Our Singapore page lists every starred restaurant with its lunch and dinner prices, and adds the service charge and GST for you.

faq.q: Which hawker stall in Singapore has a Michelin star?
faq.a: Only one: Hill Street Tai Hwa Pork Noodle on Crawford Lane, which has held one star since the first Singapore guide in 2016. Its bak chor mee costs from {{dinner:hill-street-tai-hwa-pork-noodle}} a bowl.

faq.q: Which are the most affordable Michelin star restaurants in Singapore?
faq.a: Hill Street Tai Hwa Pork Noodle, from {{dinner:hill-street-tai-hwa-pork-noodle}} a bowl, by a long way. After it come weekday set lunches: {{cheapLunchName_singapore}} from {{cheapLunchPrice_singapore}} and Lei Garden from {{lunch:lei-garden}}, both before service and GST.

faq.q: Do you need to book a Michelin star hawker stall?
faq.a: You can’t. Hawker stalls don’t take bookings: you join the queue, order and pay at the counter. Go mid-afternoon on a weekday for the shortest wait.

If you want to taste what a Michelin star means at the smallest scale, yes: it is the cheapest starred meal in the world, cooked bowl by bowl. If you are short of time, the Bib Gourmand hawkers above have shorter queues.
About S$10 to S$20 a person covers a bowl and a drink. Many hawker stalls now take PayNow and other QR payments, but carry some cash in case.

faq.q: Is there a Michelin star chicken rice in Singapore?
faq.a: Not any more. Hawker Chan’s soy sauce chicken rice lost its star in 2021. Tian Tian and Margaret Drive Sin Kee, two Hainanese chicken rice stalls, are Bib Gourmands.

faq.q: Where can I eat Michelin star dim sum in Singapore?
faq.a: At lunch in the starred Cantonese restaurants. Lei Garden’s lunch set costs {{lunch:lei-garden}} before service and GST, and Summer Pavilion at the Ritz-Carlton is also known for its dim sum.
